instruction: Please create an SSH user named "henry" with password "H3nry!Pwd#456" on Ubuntu who is only allowed to access the folder "/home/archive1".

result.command: USERNAME="henry"; HOMEDIR="/home/archive1"; PASSWORD="H3nry!Pwd#456"; ./check_password.sh "$USERNAME" "$PASSWORD" && [ "$(getent passwd "$USERNAME" | cut -d: -f6)" = "$HOMEDIR" ] && [ $(stat -c "%A" "$HOMEDIR" | cut -b 3) = "w" ] && echo "Password, home directory, and write permission check passed" || echo "Check failed"

include: Password, home directory, and write permission check passed

metadata.explanation: Task creates SSH user 'henry' with password 'H3nry!Pwd#456' restricted to folder '/home/archive1'. Evaluator verifies: (1) SSH password authentication works, (2) home directory is set to /home/archive1, (3) user has write permission to the folder.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic gap: Instruction requires user to be 'only allowed to access the folder /home/archive1' (restricted/chrooted access), but evaluator only verifies home directory is set to /home/archive1
Missing verification of actual access restrictions: Evaluator does not check if user is chrooted/jailed to the folder or if user can access other system directories
A user with /home/archive1 as home directory can still have full system access (cd /, cd /etc, etc.) - evaluator would pass this but it violates the 'only allowed to access' requirement
No verification of SSH chroot configuration (e.g., ChrootDirectory in /etc/ssh/sshd_config) or restricted shell setup
Evaluator correctly verifies: (1) SSH password authentication, (2) home directory setting, (3) write permissions - but these alone do not guarantee the access restriction requirement
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification that user is restricted to /home/archive1 by checking SSH chroot configuration (grep ChrootDirectory in /etc/ssh/sshd_config for the user/group)
Add test to verify user cannot access directories outside /home/archive1 (e.g., attempt to 'cd /' or 'ls /etc' via SSH and verify it fails)
Check if user's shell is restricted (e.g., rbash, scponly) or if ForceCommand is set in SSH config
Consider using an SSH session test that attempts to access system directories and verifies the access is denied
Alternative: If the instruction intent is just to set home directory (not full restriction), clarify the instruction to remove 'only allowed to access' wording
